"$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"

# gh-1004: [CRAP] createRepoTasks.action (181) + createRepoTasksMulti.action (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/createRepoTasks.js::action` **180.9** and `js/createRepoTasksMulti.js::action` **57.2** create per-repo tasks from the story decomposition (dedupe, links, per-tracker payloads).

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

# gh-1004: [CRAP] createRepoTasks.action (181) + createRepoTasksMulti.action (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/createRepoTasks.js::action` **180.9** and `js/createRepoTasksMulti.js::action` **57.2** create per-repo tasks from the story decomposition (dedupe, links, per-tracker payloads).

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

        id: baseline

          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

This PR updates it — scope creep + hygiene. Should be reverted and the file untracked. IMPORTANT.

2. Behavior preservation check — verify by comparing to original line-by-line. Key subtle points:

Single file:
- Original: on create error, `created.push({repo, key: null, error, depends_on: []})` — new same.
- Original: `created.push({repo, key, summary, depends_on: repo.depends_on || []})` — new same.
- Original wire loop, comment posting — same.
- Exports: expanded but superset — backward compatible.

One subtle diff: in the original single version, `extractCreatedKey` equivalent: `parsed && (parsed.key || parsed.id) ? (parsed.key || parsed.id) : null`. New: same.

Multi file:
- Original comment building was inside try around postComment; new builds comment outside try then posts inside try. buildSummaryComment can't throw realistically (String ops). Same behavior.
- Original: `createdKey = typeof result === 'string' ? (result || null) : (result && (result.key || result.id)) || null;` — new extractCreatedKey: same.

3. Check `decideDuplicate` in multi: `existingSummaries.indexOf(summary) !== -1` — unchanged.

4. Behavior-parity concern: In the multi action, original: `var tasks = topologicalSortTasks(flatenTasks(repos));` — new: `buildTaskPlan(repos)`. Same.

5. One thing to check: flattenTasks/topologicalSortTasks were NOT part of the refactor diff (pre-existing on main), unchanged.

6. Line in single createSubTasks: note original code computed summary AFTER duplicate check? No — original computed summary before the duplicate check (truncateSummary first, then duplicate check). New code also: `var summary = buildRepoSummary(...)` before `decideDuplicate`. Same. Good (summary computed even when skipped, harmless).

7. Check ticket says "helpers must be ≤ 8 CRAP". Helpers are exported for tests. Fine.

8. Check the run_createRepoTasks.json files match conventions of other run_*.json files (name JSRunner, testRunner.js). Yes.

9. Duplication dimension: two files now share large duplicated helpers (parseAffectedRepos, getJiraBaseUrl, jiraLink, loadExistingSummaries, createSubTasks, linkDependency, moveToBlocked, wireDependencies, postSummaryComment, buildSummaryComment, extractCreatedKey...) — PR description explicitly says "Helpers stay per-module (existing duplication style); no new cross-file requires, so pack closure/require-gate are untouched." So intentional, justified in description. Mention as SUGESTION maybe — extracting shared helpers to js/common/ would violate the require-gate? They said no new cross-file requires to keep pack closure untouched. So the duplication is deliberate. I can note it as a SUGESTION-level observation.

10. Check the network guard concern in tests: `file_read` global used in test guard test — file_read is real, fine.

11. Check tests don't hit real services: they mock via loadModule. OK.

12. Potential issue in test: `test('module.exports is guarded...')` reads the source file and asserts contains 'typeof module' — brittle string-only test but matches repo patterns probably.

13. Security: JQL injection via parentKey — `'parent = ' + parentKey` — pre-existing pattern, parentKey comes from Jira itself. Not new.

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

        run: |

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Session runtime artifact committed — revert and untrack**

This PR updates `.fah/bash_jobs/running.json`, which is live fa-session runtime state, not source. The new content leaks the developer's local environment into git history — a local home path (`/Users/uladzimir_klyshevich/git/dmtools-agents`), full agent shell-command history, and PIDs — and it is pure churn unrelated to the gh-1004 refactor (scope creep in a ticket that demands an unchanged-behavior refactor).

`.fah/` was added to `.gitignore` in #997 precisely to stop tracking these artifacts, but the files committed before that change are still tracked, so every local session keeps dirtying this path.

**Fix before merge:**
```bash
git rm -q --cached .fah/bash_jobs/running.json
git checkout origin/main -- .fah/bash_jobs/running.json   # or simply: git checkout -- .fah/
echo '.fah/' >> /dev/null   # already ignored; the rm --cached is the missing piece
```
Consider untracking the remaining `.fah/bash_jobs/*.log` files (still tracked from before #997) in the same pass so the diff stays clean forever.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Duplicated helper set between createRepoTasks.js and createRepoTasksMulti.js**

The two modules now each carry near-identical copies of ~10 helpers: `decideDuplicate`, `buildSummaryComment`, `extractCreatedKey`, `loadExistingSummaries`, `createSubTasks`, `linkDependency`, `moveToBlocked`, `wireDependencies`, `postSummaryComment`, plus the pre-existing `parseAffectedRepos`/`getJiraBaseUrl`/`jiraLink`. Every future fix (e.g. the 255-char truncation or dedup-key semantics) has to be made twice, and the two copies have already drifted once (`decideDuplicate` matches a repo tag substring in one file and the exact summary in the other; `extractCreatedKey` parses JSON strings in one and passes them through in the other).

I acknowledge the PR description's justification — no new cross-file requires keeps the pack closure/require-gate untouched, and this mirrors the pre-existing style. No action needed in this PR; worth a follow-up ticket to extract a shared `js/common/repoTasksShared.js` once the pack-closure rules allow it (or to extend the require-gate's allowlist deliberately), so the next behavioral fix lands in one place.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Two small test gaps in the new characterization suites**

The new helper tests are thorough, but two branches of the extracted code are exercised only implicitly or not at all:

1. `createSubTasks` in `js/createRepoTasks.js` has an early return `if (!repoName) return;` (falsy/missing `name` on a repo entry) that no test hits — a one-liner with a repo entry like `{ }` or `{ name: '' }` would pin it.
2. In both `postSummaryComment` tests the failure-swallow case is invoked (`t2.postComment = function() { throw ... }`) but never asserted — the test passes as long as no exception escapes, which is the actual contract, so this is fine; an explicit comment or a captured `console.warn` assertion would document intent.

Neither affects the CRAP outcome materially (the branches pre-existed in the inline code and the helpers stay well under threshold with current coverage), so this is polish only.

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

"$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

content.text:
Review complete. **Verdict: APPROVE** (1 important, 2 suggestions, 0 blocking — `issueCounts.blocking: 0`, consistent with the machine protocol).

## What I verified

- **Behaviour parity** — diffed both refactored modules against `origin/main` line-by-line: log lines, tracker call order (getIssue → getIssue → searchIssues → creates → links/moves → comment), return shapes, and exports (superset, backward compatible) are all identical. `extractCreatedKey`, `decideDuplicate`, truncation and dedup semantics preserved exactly, including the deliberate single-vs-multi divergence.
- **Tests** — ran both new run files (`36 passed, 0 failed` and `37 passed, 0 failed`) and the full canonical harness: **3640 passed, 0 failed**, matching the PR description precisely. No `istanbul ignore`, no deleted tests, no lazy requires (pack closure safe), GraalJS style (`var`, no arrows) respected, tests wired into `run_all.json` per AGENTS.md.
- **Conventions** — the `typeof module` export guard is kept and pinned by tests (matches repo pattern), session-state file handling checked.

## Findings

1. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — `.fah/bash_jobs/running.json` (in the diff at line 1): a live session runtime artifact re-committed with local paths and agent command history; `.fah/` was gitignored in #997 but remains tracked. Should be reverted and `git rm --cached`.
2. 💡 **SUGGESTION** — ~10 near-identical helpers duplicated across the two modules (justified by pack-closure constraint; follow-up extraction candidate).
3. 💡 **SUGGESTION** — two minor test gaps: falsy `repoName` early-return in `createSubTasks` untested; comment-swallow case invoked but unasserted.
